title: The Many Faces of 了
description: Completed actions, new situations, 'not anymore', 快…了, 已经…了, durations with one or two 了, and 了吗 questions.

points.title: Verb + 了 + object: completed action
points.summary: 了 right after the verb marks a completed action. A quantified object (三杯, 一本) usually follows.
points.body:
- 他喝**了**三杯咖啡.
- 我买**了**一本书.
- Negative: 没 + verb, **without** 了 (我没买书).
examples: He drank three cups of coffee.

points.title: Sentence + 了: change / new situation
points.summary: 了 at the end of a sentence says 'now it's like this' — something has changed.
points.body:
- 下雨**了**! (It's started raining!)
- 我饿**了** (I'm hungry now).
- 不 + verb + 了 = not anymore: 我不喝酒**了**.

points.title: 快(要) + verb + 了: about to
points.summary: 快 / 快要 + verb/adj + 了 = something is about to happen. The 了 is required.

points.title: Verb + 了 + duration (+ 了)
points.summary: One 了: the action lasted that long (finished). Two 了: it has lasted that long **so far** and is still going.
points.body:
- 我学**了**两年中文 (I studied for two years — maybe I've stopped).
- 我学**了**两年中文**了** (I've been studying for two years — and still am).
examples: I've been learning Chinese for two years now.

points.title: Verb + 了吗? / 还没(有)
points.summary: Did you …? = verb + 了吗? Answer: verb + 了 / 还没(有) (not yet).
points.body: - 你吃饭**了吗**? — 吃了 / 还没有.

questions.prompt: {我|wǒ}{昨天|zuótiān}{买|mǎi}（　）{一|yì}{本|běn}{书|shū}，{今天|jīntiān}{已经|yǐjīng}{看|kàn}{完|wán}{了|le}。
notes: 着 marks a lasting state, not a finished purchase.
在 goes before the verb.
买的一本书 would need a noun after it in a different structure.
questions.translation: I bought a book yesterday and finished reading it today.

notes: 了 can't split the measure word and the noun.
了 comes after the verb, not before it.
了 can't split the number and the measure word.
questions.translation: He drank three cups of coffee.

notes: 下雨着 isn't natural.
下雨过 = 'it has rained before' — not a new situation.
的 doesn't mark a change.
questions.translation: It's started raining! Let's hurry home.

notes: That's 我还没喝.
That's 我没喝酒.
That's 我从来没喝过酒.
正在 doesn't combine with 了 like this.
If it had already left, you couldn't get on.
刚开了 isn't the pattern — and you couldn't get on either.
questions.translation: The train is about to leave — get on quickly!

notes: 快 goes before the verb.
了 goes at the end.
快 needs the final 了.
还吃过饭了 isn't grammatical.
正在 = 'in the middle of' — clashes with 过…了.
快吃过饭了 isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: I've already eaten, I'm not hungry.

notes: 一直走 = 'go straight / keep walking'.
正在走了 isn't grammatical.
从来 needs a negative.
questions.translation: He's already left — come back tomorrow.

questions.prompt: {我|wǒ}{学|xué}（　）{两|liǎng}{年|nián}{中文|Zhōngwén}，{现在|xiànzài}{能|néng}{看|kàn}{懂|dǒng}{一点儿|yìdiǎnr}。
notes: 学的两年 isn't the pattern.
着 doesn't take a duration like this.
在 goes before the verb.
questions.translation: I studied Chinese for two years and can now understand a little.

questions.prompt: Which sentence says you are **still** learning (two years so far)?
notes: 过 = at some point in the past.
One 了 = it lasted two years (could be over).
The duration goes after the verb.
questions.translation: I've been learning Chinese for two years now.

notes: The order is 了吗.
过了 doesn't make a question.
了呢 doesn't ask a yes/no question.
questions.translation: A: Have you eaten? B: Yes.

notes: 还不了 isn't an answer.
No 了 after 还没有.
还不 doesn't answer 'did you?'.
questions.translation: A: Have you bought the tickets? B: Not yet.
